title: Non-uniqueness for a differential equation
summary: Let $f(t,x),M(t,x)\in C([0,1]^2)$ with $M(t,x)>0$. We consider differential equations of the form \[ \frac{\partial f}{\partial t}(t,x)=\frac{M(t,x)f(t,x)-M(t,0)f(t,0)}{x},\quad x>0. \] For a fixed positive weight $M$, we ask whether the condition $f(0,x)=0$ forces $f\equiv 0$. We show the answer is negative for smooth functions: there exist $f(t,x),M(t,x)\in C^{\infty}([0,1]^2)$ with $f(0,x)=0$, $f(t,0)\not\equiv 0$, and $M(t,x)>0$ satisfying the above equation.
